requirements.summary: The installed rule declares daily rotation, parses as an after-1-day policy, and the enabled, active logrotate timer shows the next daily run. A forced run directly demonstrated that the rule rotates the target log.

requirements.requirement: Keep seven compressed rotations of the application log.
requirements.summary: The parsed policy specifies seven rotations with compression. The behavioral test produced a valid app.log.1.gz, and the policy plus compressed data remained intact after restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation.
requirements.summary: A writer kept the log descriptor open across rotation. Its pre-rotation marker appeared in the compressed file, its post-rotation marker appeared in the active log, and the active inode remained unchanged. Writing also succeeded after node restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The node-restart protocol is also complete: healthy policy, timer, and log state were captured before restart; restart was acknowledged; the boot ID changed from 1e0cb179-d384-41f8-aa25-9390b31eec45 to 66ac79c4-ceed-4a52-b09a-cd4b077c0957; and system health, timer operation, policy, compressed data, and log writes recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate that transition.
limitations: Only one rotation was executed, so deletion after exceeding seven historical rotations was not directly exercised; the retention result relies on the successfully parsed rotate-7 semantics.
The next naturally scheduled daily execution was not awaited; daily cadence is supported by the parsed rule and active system timer, while actual rotation behavior was demonstrated with a forced run.
Writer continuity was tested with a controlled held-open file descriptor because no persistent inventory application process or service was present in the captured baseline.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing the policy was the required implementation; the forced rotation, temporary writer markers, and post-restart write were bounded functional evidence; and the reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol. Temporary synchronization files did not remain after reboot. Final snapshots show no failed services, damaged package state, or material new exposure.
